beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:setting the scene, intrigued]In {1923|nineteen twenty-three}, a geologist looked at a scarred land in the north-west of the United States, and said a ^*flood* carved it in ^days.
[d:tension][act:dry, a rueful smile][tune:fall]His colleagues ^laughed at him for ^forty years.

[d:calm][act:warm, introducing him]His name was J Harlen ^Bretz. [act:wonder, seeing it through his eyes]He saw dry ^waterfalls, giant ^ripples like the ones on a beach, only ^huge, and canyons with ^no river to cut them.

[d:build][go:2|0][act:relishing the numbers]Take Dry ^Falls: five and a half kilometres ^wide, a hundred and twenty-one metres ^high. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a comparison]Niagara Falls is less than one kilometre wide, and less than half as ^tall. [sfx:shimmer][act:delighted, building]Seven Niagaras, side by side, would fit along its ^edge. [d:aside][act:quick, playful aside, lower][tune:fall]Which is a ^rude thing to say to Niagara.

[d:build][act:explaining, curious]But where could so much water come ^from? [p:0.93][act:explaining, building the picture]An Ice Age ^lake in Montana, held back by a ^wall of ice. [go:4|0][p:0.93][act:vivid, the scale]That wall stood ^six hundred metres tall: as tall as a two-hundred-storey ^building.

[d:list][p:0.93][act:explaining, a neat bit of physics]Now, ice ^floats. [act:explaining, clear]As the lake rose, it lifted the dam like a ^cork, and two and a half ^thousand cubic kilometres of water burst out across the ^state. [act:leaning in][tune:fallrise]And not ^once. [act:the punch, slower][tune:fall]About ^*forty* times. [go:5|0][p:0.93][gap:0.4][act:curious, the method]How do we ^know? [act:explaining, an everyday picture]Downstream, each flood left a bed of sand and ^silt, stacked like ^pages. [act:explaining, the clincher]Between them lie animal ^burrows and volcanic ^ash: years passed between the ^floods.

[d:build][act:matter of fact, curious]When did they ^run? [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]The floods left great ^boulders lying in the ^open. [act:explaining, an everyday picture]Rays from space slowly build up rare atoms in their ^surface, a bit like a ^suntan. [p:0.9][act:the key idea, slower]Measure the tan, and you know how long each boulder has lain ^there: [act:matter of fact, precise]roughly ^eighteen thousand to ^fourteen thousand seven hundred years.

[d:reveal][act:warm, a vindication story]In {1979|nineteen seventy-nine}, at ^ninety-six, Bretz got geology's highest ^medal. [act:quoting him, mischievous]His reply: [sfx:hit]all my enemies are ^dead, so I have no one to ^gloat over.

[d:calm][go:8|0][act:even, reporting a newer idea]Some now go ^further, and tie the biggest floods to a ^comet, at the start of a sudden cold spell called the Younger ^Dryas, about twelve thousand nine hundred years ago. [d:aside][act:a careful caveat, lower]That needs a flood bed dated to that ^moment. [act:plain, open-minded][tune:fallrise]^None has been found, yet.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]The ^floods? [act:firm, certain][tune:highfall]^*Established*. [act:vivid, tracing it]From the ice dam all the way to the ^Pacific, in ^days. [act:the next question, even][tune:rise]A ^comet behind them? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]Still awaiting ^evidence.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:grounded, fair][tune:fall]Catastrophes are ^real. [act:the last word, a knowing smile][tune:fall]The trick is telling ^*which* one.
